newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister doubts shift in British EU policy.
newsitem.headline: French minister doubts shift in British EU policy.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette on Sunday predicted little change in Britain's European policy after the May 1 election but praised the opposition Labour Party as being infinitely more modern than France's Socialists.
"I am not sure that Britain's position on European affairs will change much depending on which camp British electors choose," he told Europe 1 radio.
"We know the Labour Party has said they would ratify the social chapter, which is an important part of the Maastricht Treaty," he said. "For the rest, we'll see what happens."
Polls predict that Tony Blair's Labour Party will win a landslide victory in Thursday's election, ousting Prime Minister John Major's Conservatives after 18 years in power.

De Charette, a centrist facing a French parliamentary election on May 25-June 1, praised Labour as having a "language infinitely more modern and, deep down, more in line with the realities of this world" than France's Socialist Party.
"It's really two different worlds," he said, pointing to French Socialist plans to create 700,000 jobs "out of a hat".
He also defended President Jacques Chirac's decision to call the snap election for the National Assembly almost 10 months early.

"It's preferable for us not to be in the situation that John Major has been in. I've seen him at successive European summits, a man campaigning and harassed by his opponents, and who thus does not have all the desirable freedom to defend the interests of his country," he said.
